newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: North and Central America port conditions -Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions -Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

EL SALVADOR, Sept 26 - Acajutla - 14 vessels due for discharging (petroleum, steel products, sulphate, containers, corn, grease and sunflower oil, vehicles, diesel oil, bulk corn, general cargo and containers). No delays expected. 1 vessel discharging rice at berth.

HONDURAS, Puerto Cortes - Sept 30 - Three vessels berthed of which 1 discharging soy, 2 loading bananas, 2 anchored of which 1 to discharge/load containers, 1 to load bananas. 12 due of which 8 to discharge/load containers, 3 to load bananas, 1 to load concentrates. No berthing delays expected. Vessels berthed 2 discharging/loading containers, 1 discharging soymeal in bulk, 1 loading bananas, 1 loading bananas/discharging containers. Vessels waiting 6 to discharge/load containers, 2 to discharge bananas, 1 steel, 1 to load containers/discharge lead. Vessels due 2 to discharge/load containers, 4 to discharge/load general, 3 to load bananas, 1 to discharge paper, 1 corn, 1 mill feed.

PANAMA, Sept 30 - Balboa - vessels operating 1 general, 1 tanker. Cristobal - vessels operating 3 general, 1 car carrier. Panama Canal - Miraflores and Gatun locks lane outages began 29/9, scheduled to complete 6/10. During this period, canal authorities project average daily transit of 28-30 vessels. Traffic experiencing 36 hours delay. 30 vessels due, 34 in queue. 16 Booked. 31 scheduled. oct 1 - vessels waiting for transit at 0001 hours 1/10 - 34 At 0001 hours. 2/10 41 at 0001 hours. 3/10 45. Delays 3 days for 91 ft beam and over, and/or restricted due to cargo/draft 2 days for under 91 ft beam. Transit schedules also being affected by seasonal fog. Booking system remains at condition 1, Panama Canal has not indicated if it will be reduced to condition 2.

UNITED STATES, Sept 30 - Jersey City, Port Newark, NJ - no vessels in ports. Port Elizabeth, NJ - four vessels in port. Perth Amboy, Bayway, Cartaret, NJ - one vessel in each. Hampton Roads, VA - six general cargo/container vessels in pier operating 1 in pier loading coal 1 bulker discharging gypsum, 1 bulker loading fertiliser, 1 anchored waiting to load 2 in pier under repairs.

HONOLULU, HI - harbour - 3 container vessels alongside, 2 tugs and barges alongside off port. anchorage - 1 tanker anchored awaiting berth. Barbers point - harbour 1 tanker loading alongside, 1 tug and barge alongside offport moorings, 1 tanker discharging crude.

BALTIMORE, MD - vessels operating in port 8 bulkers, 5 containers, 2 ro/ro, 2 auto vessels, 2 tankers, 4 general cargo 2 cable vessels on standby, 4 in repair yard 5 bulkers awaiting berth of which 1 to discharge alumina billets, 3 to discharge sugar, 1 other vessel.

COLUMBIA RIVER, Oct 1 - Congestion mild, grain vessels up to 2 days berthing delay. Astoria - no vessels anchored. Portland - five grain vessels anchored, 1 loading, 4 under repairs, 1 container alongside, 1 cement, 2 tankers, 1 alumina discharging. Vancouver, wa - one grain vessel loading, 2 general cargo discharging. Kalama - no vessels loading. Longview - three log vessels loading.

EAST COAST, BALTIMORE, MD - No congestion expected at Dundalk terminal this week. Elevators and coal operations working normally, no delays. Average waiting time consol coal 6 days liquid bulk facilities operating normally, no berthing congestion. Anchorage clear at Baltimore and Annapolis.

CHARLESTON, SC - No vessels due at either shipyard river coal terminal or grain elevator, no delays expected at tanker terminals. All terminals working well. Columbus street, Wando, and North Charleston terminals will be light. Georgetown terminal no delays. Dredging taking place throughout week. No navigation problems in harbour.
MIAMI, FL - berths availability for container, ro/ro and bulk vessels. Passenger terminals full.
NEW YORK - No congestion at anchorages, container, tanker terminals. Congestion continues at Brooklyn sugar terminal at Yonkers sugar terminal.

NORFOLK, VA - 18 vessels due at Norfolk southern coal pier, 2 anchored waiting to load, 5 due at Dominion terminal, 3 due at Pier ix coal terminal in week. No vessels anchored waiting to load. Norfolk southern scheduled maintenance from 1/10 to 9/10 during period one shiploader will be operating. No vessels due at Cargill, no delays at container and general cargo terminals, oil and bulk terminals working normally, all channels opening with prevailing depths available.
PHILADELPHIA, PA - no congestion in ports of Philadelphia, Camden, Wilmington. No activity as far as dredging, repairs, navigational problems.

SAVANNAH, GA - no congestion expected at Georgia Port Authorities garden city terminals throughout week, nor at ocean terminals. Liquid bulk facilities operating normally, no berth congestion expected. 1-2 days delay expected at Colonial Marine terminals for bulk clay due to berth congestion and mechanical difficulties at terminal. Vessels with weather sensitive cargo may expect some downtime due to rain. some delays due to periods of fog, all navigational conditions remain normal.

GULF COAST, Houston, Tx - no congestion at city docks, Cargill grain elevator and public grain elevator. Waiting time reduced to 2 days at Farmland grain elevator, Galveston. Mobile, Al - private and state-owned terminals operating normally. Alabama state docks coal terminal maintenance dredging commenced 27/9 at berth no. 2. Expected to be completed in 8-10 days.

NEW ORLEANS, LA - Rain delays in cargo operations, especially grain loading. Grain shipments slow river stage at 3.1 feet, normal transit times can be expected. Max permissible draft at sw pass 47 ft. FW for vessels under 100,000 dwt, 46 ft FW for vessels over 100,000 dwt. Some elevators not working at weekends due to slower than usual grain shipments.

WEST COAST, Columbia River - newly built Campotex facility at terminal 5, Portland, expected to be on line sometime in first quarter 1997, to commence export of potash products from Columbia river. Expected to bring additional vessel traffic into Columbia River, Portland area. 15 vessels in port, 6 loading, 9 waiting, 3-4 days average waiting time. Coos Bay - one lumber vessel at ocean terminals, 2 vessels at export service, 2 log vessels, 1 nickel ore at Glenbrook nickel dock, 2 linerboard vessels loading for discharge in China. Traffic conditions good.

Long Beach, CA - Metropolitan busy for October, delays of 2 days expected at anchor awaiting berth. Koch Carbon 1 vessel scheduled for month. Kaiser up to 2 days berthing delay for coal/petcoke. Moderately light for bulk cargoes in the Los Angles, Long Beach harbour. Seattle - no berthing congestion at Puget Sound grain elevators.
